Lemma 6, Eqs. (11)–(13). Starting with row sparsity d and entry bound b>0, Hermiticity gives column sparsity. The constructed isometry and self-adjoint unitary swap compress to H/(db). The construction is in matrix frames.

From a d-row-sparse Hermitian H with entry magnitudes at most b, one segmented QSP word simulates physical time τ/(db) for rational τ on every input with relative vector-norm error at most 2⁻ᵏ. Both counts belong to that word and charge its walk oracle and exact matrix gates. Theorem 3 (2017) counts elementary gates and position/entry queries with an optimal truncation schedule.

Lemma 6, Eqs. (11)–(13), in frames. Row and column sparsity d and entry bound b yield isometries with overlap H/(db), related by a self-adjoint unitary swap. The declaration constructs the encoding mathematically.

For an existing projected unitary encoding, a segmented, amplified QSP word approximates the time-evolution action on the embedded input. Its exact oracle and fixed-matrix gate counts use its own cutoff and segment parameters.

Appendix A, Theorem 1(3), with a uniform-clock phase-estimation variant. For a Hermitian A with all eigenvalue magnitudes in [d,1/4], a single run with clock M=max(2,⌈65536/(d⁶ε⁴)⌉) succeeds with probability at least d²/4. The postselected state is within ε of normalized A⁻¹b in the clean success registers. Its circuit uses 2(M−1) exact spectral-oracle queries and 4(M−1)+6 fixed-matrix gates.

For signed gapped spectral data the uniform-clock reciprocal filter has Born success at least d²/4 and normalized pseudoinverse-state error at most 2η/d when M ≥ 4096/(d²η⁴) and η ≤ d/2. These are variant-specific precision bounds.
